cues.text: Hello, Picturerep. Can I help you?
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Oh, hi. I saw your advertisement about copying pictures to disk and I'd like a bit more information about what you do.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Sure. What would you like to know?
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Well, I've got a box full of old family photos that's been up in the attic for years, some of them must be 50 or 60 years old, and I'd like to get them converted to digital format.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Sure, we can do that for you.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Right. And what about size? The photos are all sorts of sizes are there any restrictions?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Well the maximum size of photo we can do with our normal service is 30 centimetres. And each picture must be at least 4 centimetres, that's the minimum we can cope with.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: That should be fine. And some of them are in a frame - should I take them out before I send them?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Yes please, we can't copy them otherwise. And also the photos must all be separate, they mustn't be stuck into an album.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: OK, that's not a problem. So can you give me an idea of how much this will cost? I've got about 360 photos I think.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: We charge £195 for 300 to 400 photos for the basic service.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: OK. And does that include the disk?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Yes, one disk - but you can get extra ones for £5 each.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: That's good. So do I need to pay when I send you the photos?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: No, we won't need anything until we've actually copied the pictures. Then we'll let you know how much it is, and once we've received the payment, we'll send the parcel off to you.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask about our services?
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Yes. I've roughly sorted out the photos into groups, according to what they're about - so can you keep them in those groups when you copy them?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Sure. We'll save each group in a different folder on the disk and if you like, you can suggest a name for each folder.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: So I could have one called 'Grandparents' for instance?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Exactly.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: And do you do anything besides scan the photos? Like, can you make any Improvements?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Yes, in the standard service each photo is checked, and we can sometimes touch up the colour a bit, or improve the contrast - that can make a big difference.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: OK. And some of the photos are actually quite fragile - they won't get damaged in the process, will they?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: No, if any look particularly fragile, we'd do them by hand. We do realise how precious these old photos can be.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Sure.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: And another thing is we can make changes to a photo if you want - so if you want to remove an object from a photo, or maybe alter the background, we can do that.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Really? I might be interested in that. I'll have a look through the photos and see. Oh, and talking of fixing photos - I've got a few that aren't properly in focus. Can you do anything to make that better?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: No, I'm afraid that's one thing we can't do.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: OK.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Any other information I can give you?
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Er ... oh, how long will it all take?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: We aim to get the copying done in ten days.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: Fine. Right, well I'll get the photos packed up in a box and post them off to you.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Right. If you've got a strong cardboard box, that's best. We've found that plastic ones sometimes break in the post.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE

cues.text: OK. Right, thanks for your help. Bye.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Bye.
cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
